options.label: Immediate Verification and Conditional Award
options.description: Verify Corvane's license status immediately and, if valid, proceed with the award while requiring a 150% performance bond to mitigate risk.

options.label: Active Cultivation and Negotiation
options.description: Delay the vote to actively negotiate a compliance bridge with Corvane, such as securing their C-16 license or bonding the risk, rather than passively waiting.

options.label: Statutory Interpretation Challenge
options.description: Challenge the absolute rigidity of Bus. & Prof. Code § 7028.15(e) by arguing for a waiver based on public safety urgency and the intent of the law.

options.label: Strategic Consortium Alignment
options.description: Invite both bidders to a joint meeting to form a consortium where Tasker & Moye handles licensed work and Corvane handles general building, aligning them with the district's deadline.

options.label: Procedural Re-bid
options.description: Reject the current bid due to the license deficiency and issue a new bid with clearer instructions to prevent future procedural failures.

options.label: Passive Delay for Verification
options.description: Simply wait for the verification of Corvane's license status before making any decision, treating time as an enemy to be beaten rather than a tool.

options.label: Immediate Verification and Conditional Award
options.note: Awarding a contract to a bidder who lacks the mandatory C-16 license for fire protection work violates Business and Professions Code § 7026.12 and § 7028.15(e), rendering the contract void ab initio regardless of bond requirements.

options.label: Active Cultivation and Negotiation
options.note: Negotiating with a bidder to obtain a license or alter bid terms after submission violates the fundamental principle of competitive bidding and constitutes an impermissible material alteration of the bid.

options.label: Statutory Interpretation Challenge
options.note: There is no statutory waiver for safety-critical licensing requirements; attempting to argue that public safety urgency overrides the C-16 mandate is legally baseless and would invite immediate litigation.

options.label: Strategic Consortium Alignment
options.note: Forming a consortium with the second-place bidder after bids are opened to fix a licensing defect constitutes bid rigging and a material change to the competitive process, violating public contract laws.

options.label: Procedural Re-bid
options.note: While legally defensible to reject a non-responsive bid and re-bid, this option fails the client's primary objective of meeting the 2027 schedule and incurs significant cost and delay.

options.label: Passive Delay for Verification
options.note: Waiting for verification is procedurally safe but fails to advance the client's schedule goals and leaves the district vulnerable to a writ of mandate from the protesting bidder.

grade.missing: An experienced practitioner would have immediately rejected Corvane's bid as non-responsive based on the clear statutory prohibition against a Class B contractor performing fire protection work without a C-16 classification, and would have advised the Board to award the contract to the next lowest responsive and responsible bidder (Tasker & Moye) or, if their bid was also flawed, to re-bid the project.
grade.overall: The provided courses of action are largely legally unsound because they attempt to cure a fatal licensing defect through negotiation, bonding, or creative interpretation, which violates California's strict public bidding laws. The only legally defensible path is to reject the non-responsive bid, but the options presented fail to balance this legal necessity with the client's urgent schedule needs by not immediately moving to the next qualified bidder.
